title: Reserve Retention Share of a Released Hazard Refund Excess
content:
**Scope.** Returned hazard premiums paid back into a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts, where part of the hazard refund excess is released.

**Rule.** The reserve's retention share is read from the Summit loan's ledger (Cedarline Summit Proprietary Reverse Mortgage):

1. A corporate advance for property tax or for insurance posted within the twenty-four months before the handling date — the reserve keeps the full retention share, 1, of the released hazard refund excess.
2. No such advance, but an occupancy inspection fee posted within the twelve months before the handling date — the reserve keeps the half retention share, 0.5, of it.
3. Neither — this rule retains nothing.

The borrower's side keeps the released hazard refund excess times one less the reserve's retention share. A posting falls within a window when it is dated no later than the handling date and fewer than 24 (or 12) whole calendar months before it; an inspection fee posted 13 months earlier does not count, while a charge advance posted 13 months earlier does.

**Hypothetical figures.** Released excess 180.00: with the full share the borrower's side keeps nothing; with the half share it keeps 90.00.
